title: Safe sleep
text: Sleep baby on her back, face and head uncovered, in a safe cot with nothing else in it, smoke-free, in your room for the first 6–12 months.

title: Car seat
text: Babies travel rear-facing in an approved restraint until at least 6 months, harness snug and untwisted. Get it professionally fitted if unsure.

title: Newborn sleep
text: Newborns sleep a lot, but in short stretches of 2–4 hours. Normal household noise is fine; you don't need a silent house.

title: Sun safety
text: Keep babies under 12 months out of direct sun. Never drape a blanket or wrap over the pram; it traps heat. Use the hood and pick shady routes.

title: Whooping cough
text: Newborns are especially vulnerable to whooping cough. Visitors should be vaccinated and wash hands before holding baby. Her first big round of vaccinations is at 6 weeks.

title: Breastfeeding in public
text: Breastfeeding in public is legal and protected in Australia. Dad's job: water, snacks, a comfy spot, and backing mum.

title: Car seat sleep
text: Car seats are for travel, not sleep. Take breaks on longer drives and move her to a safe sleep space when you arrive.

title: Hot car
text: Never leave a baby alone in a car, even for a minute; cars heat up fast. And if you're too tired to drive safely, don't drive.

title: Bath time
text: Never leave a baby alone in the bath, even for a second. Check the water with your wrist or elbow, or a bath thermometer at about 37–38°C.

title: Tired signs
text: Watch for tired signs like yawning, grizzling, jerky movements and staring. Settling is much easier before she's overtired.

title: Change table
text: Always keep one hand on baby on a change table. Have everything ready before you start.

title: Starting solids
text: Start solids at around 6 months, not before 4 months. Watch for readiness: good head control, sitting with support, interest in your food. Introduce common allergy foods like egg and peanut in the first year.

title: Teething
text: A cold (not frozen) teething ring helps. Avoid amber teething necklaces; they're a choking and strangulation risk.

title: Advice changes
text: Baby advice has changed since their day; for example, babies now sleep on their backs. Share today's guidance kindly.

title: Button batteries
text: Button batteries can be deadly if swallowed. Keep them locked away, and go to hospital immediately if you suspect one has been swallowed. Anchor furniture to walls so it can't tip.

title: Separation
text: Separation anxiety is normal around this age. A short, consistent goodbye routine works better than sneaking out.

title: Dad wellbeing
text: You made it. Look after yourself too: dads can experience perinatal anxiety and depression, and PANDA supports dads as well as mums.
